# File type filtering

File type filtering lives in the `ignore` crate, in two modules: `crates/ignore/src/types.rs` (the machinery) and `crates/ignore/src/default_types.rs` (the data). Nothing else in the workspace implements type matching; `crates/core` only translates flags into builder calls.

## How definitions are represented

A definition is a name plus a list of globs:

```rust
pub struct FileTypeDef {
    name: String,
    globs: Vec<String>,
}
```

That's the whole model. There's no extension list, no content sniffing, no MIME table — a "type" is a name bound to globs, and membership is decided by matching a path's file name against them.

The defaults are a flat const table in `default_types.rs`:

```rust
pub(crate) const DEFAULT_TYPES: &[(&[&str], &[&str])] = &[
    (&["ada"], &["*.adb", "*.ads"]),
    (&["bat", "batch"], &["*.bat"]),
    ...
];
```

The first slice is names, the second is globs. Multiple names in the first slice are aliases, but only in the sense that `add_defaults` loops over the cross product and calls `add(name, glob)` once per pair. There's no alias indirection at runtime: `bat` and `batch` become two independent `FileTypeDef` values with identical globs, and both show up separately in `--type-list`. Note that globs are file-name globs, not path globs — `matched` extracts the file name before matching, so a definition like `*.rs` and a definition like `src/*.rs` behave the same way (the latter can never match).

`TypesBuilder` holds definitions in a `HashMap<String, FileTypeDef>` keyed by name, and selections in a separate `Vec<Selection<()>>`. Definitions and selections are independent: defining a type does not select it, and `build()` only compiles globs for types that were actually selected or negated.

## How the matcher is built

`TypesBuilder::build()` walks `self.selections` in order. For each selection it looks up the named definition — a miss is `Error::UnrecognizedFileType` — and then adds every glob of that definition to a `GlobSetBuilder` with `literal_separator(true)`. As it goes it pushes `(isel, iglob)` onto `glob_to_selection`, so glob index *i* in the compiled `GlobSet` maps back to the selection that contributed it.

That parallel-index trick is the load-bearing part of the design. `Types::matched` calls `GlobSet::matches_into`, which returns matching glob indices **in ascending order**, and then takes `matches.last()`. Because `glob_to_selection` was built in selection order, the highest glob index is the *last* selection on the command line that matched. Precedence is therefore last-flag-wins, and it falls out of the index ordering rather than from any explicit comparison. If you ever reorder how globs are added to the set, you break precedence silently.

The rest of `matched` is small and worth reading in full:

- Directories never match; `is_dir` returns `Match::None` immediately, as does an empty glob set.
- `has_selected` is precomputed at build time as "at least one non-negated selection exists." When it's true, a non-match becomes `Match::Ignore(Glob::unmatched())` rather than `Match::None` — this is what makes `-t rust` a whitelist instead of a mere preference.
- `pathutil::file_name` returns `None` for paths ending in `.`, `..`, or empty; that case follows the same `has_selected` rule.
- A matching selection yields `Match::Whitelist` or `Match::Ignore` depending on `Selection::is_negated`.

`Types` also carries `matches: Arc<Pool<Vec<usize>>>` from `regex_automata`'s pool, so the per-match scratch vector isn't reallocated on every path during a parallel walk. Keep that in mind if you add state to `Types`: it's cloned per worker in `dir.rs`.

## Where it plugs in

`crates/core/flags/hiargs.rs::types()` builds the matcher. It calls `add_defaults()` and then replays `low.type_changes` — a single `Vec<TypeChange>` covering `--type-clear`, `--type-add`, `-t/--type` and `-T/--type-not` — in argument order, which is why `--type-clear cpp --type-add 'cpp:*.foo'` works but the reverse doesn't.

The result reaches the walker via `WalkBuilder::types` → `IgnoreBuilder::types`, stored as `Arc<Types>`. In `Ignore::matched` (`crates/ignore/src/dir.rs:399`), types are consulted **last**: `-g/--glob` overrides win outright, then ignore-file rules, then types. That ordering is what the `-t` documentation means by "lower precedence than both the --glob flag and any rules found in ignore files."

## What to know before changing this

- **`add` validates names, not globs.** A name must be non-empty, not `all`, and every character must satisfy `char::is_alphanumeric`; otherwise you get `Error::InvalidDefinition`. Glob syntax errors surface later, at `build()`, as `Error::Glob`.
- **`include` is a snapshot, not a reference.** `add_def("bar:include:foo,cpp")` clones the globs of `foo` and `cpp` into `bar` right then. Adding globs to `foo` afterwards does not update `bar`. `add_def` also validates all included names up front so a partial failure can't mutate state — `test_invalid_defs` asserts exactly that.
- **`select("all")` / `negate("all")` iterate `HashMap` keys**, so the relative order of the pushed selections is unspecified. Don't write code (or tests) that depends on which `FileTypeDef` gets reported when several match under `--type=all`.
- **`clear(name)` removes the definition outright.** A later `select` on that name fails at `build()` rather than matching nothing.
- **Adding a default type** means editing `DEFAULT_TYPES` only. Keep it sorted by first name — `default_types_are_sorted` enforces it — and wrapped to 79 columns. Overlapping globs across types are fine and common (`*.cs` appears under both `cs` and `csharp`).
DOCEOF

Written to `<path> (812 words). Nothing else touched on disk.

The document covers three sections, all grounded in the source:

**Representation** — `FileTypeDef` is just `{ name: String, globs: Vec<String> }`; `DEFAULT_TYPES` in `crates/ignore/src/default_types.rs` is a flat `&[(&[&str], &[&str])]` table. Aliases like `("bat", "batch")` aren't indirection — `add_defaults` expands the cross product into two independent defs, which is why both appear in `--type-list`.

**Construction** — the interesting part is `glob_to_selection: Vec<(usize, usize)>`, built in selection order alongside the `GlobSetBuilder`. Since `matches_into` returns indices in ascending order and `matched` takes `matches.last()`, last-flag-wins precedence is an emergent property of index ordering, not an explicit rule. Also documented: `has_selected` as the whitelist switch that turns a non-match into `Match::Ignore`, and the `Arc<Pool<Vec<usize>>>` scratch buffer.

**Contributor notes** — name validation is alphanumeric-only and happens in `add` while glob errors surface at `build()`; `include` copies globs at definition time rather than referencing them; `select("all")` iterates `HashMap` keys so ordering is unspecified; `clear` makes a later `select` a hard `build()` error; and the `default_types_are_sorted` test constrains how you add defaults.

Two notes on what I found while reading:

- The wiring in `crates/core/flags/hiargs.rs:1177` replays all four type flags from one ordered `Vec<TypeChange>`, so `--type-clear cpp --type-add 'cpp:*.foo'` and the reverse are genuinely different commands. I included this because it's the kind of thing that looks like a bug report until you see the single vec.
- I noted the `-g/--glob` → ignore-files → types precedence chain from `crates/ignore/src/dir.rs:399`, since it's what the `-t` man page assertion actually rests on.
